body.name: Empirical tail and joint-mark calibration
body.construction:
With \(t_n=n^{-\beta}\), define the raw cross-fitted count
\[
 \widehat T(t)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n A_i\mathbf 1\{\widehat e_i\leq t\}
\]
and its positive version \(\widehat T_+(t)=\max\{\widehat T(t),n^{-2}\}\).  Put
\[
 \widetilde\alpha=\frac{\log\{\widehat T_+(2t_n)/\widehat T_+(t_n)\}}{\log2},\qquad
 \widehat\alpha=\Pi_{[1+\kappa_-/2,(3+\kappa_+)/2]}(\widetilde\alpha),
\]
\[
 \widehat K=\max\!\left\{n^{-2},\frac{\widehat T_+(t_n)}{t_n^{\widehat\alpha}}\right\},
 \qquad \widehat a_n=(n\widehat K)^{1/\widehat\alpha}.
\]
If the selected set \(\{i:A_i=1,\widehat e_i\leq t_n\}\) is nonempty, let \(\widehat H\) be the empirical law on that set of
\[
 \bigl(Y_i-\widehat\mu_1(X_i),\widehat\mu_1(X_i)-\widehat\mu_0(X_i)\bigr);
\]
otherwise set \(\widehat H\) to the point mass at \((0,0)\).  The truncations and fallback make the calibration a measurable total map and are inactive with probability tending to one uniformly on the declared class.
